en: I met my school friend by chance at the railway station yesterday.
tamil: நேத்து ரயில்வே ஸ்டேஷன்ல என் ஸ்கூல் ஃப்ரெண்டை தற்செயலா பார்த்தேன்.
context: Telling a family member about a surprise meeting.
explain: 'By chance' means it was not planned. 'Met' is the past of 'meet'.
usage: Use it to share a pleasant surprise with family or colleagues.
leelaQ: Have you met an old friend suddenly somewhere?
answer: Yes, I met my classmate in a supermarket after ten years.

en: Let me finish my story first.
tamil: முதல்ல என் கதையை முடிக்க விடுங்க.
context: Politely stopping an interruption.
explain: 'Let me' asks for permission or space to do something.
usage: Use it politely when someone keeps interrupting you.
leelaQ: What do you do when someone interrupts you?
answer: I politely ask them to let me finish.

en: The train was late, so we reached the function after the muhurtham.
tamil: ரயில் லேட்டா வந்ததால முகூர்த்தம் முடிஞ்சப்புறம்தான் விழாவுக்கு போனோம்.
context: Explaining why you missed part of a wedding.
explain: 'Was late' describes the train. 'So' shows the result of that delay.
usage: Use it to explain to relatives why you came late to an event.
leelaQ: Have you ever reached an event very late?
answer: Yes, I reached a friend's party after the cake cutting.

en: She didn't call me back after the interview.
tamil: இன்டர்வியூக்கு அப்புறம் அவங்க என்னை திரும்ப கூப்பிடல.
context: Telling a friend about a job application.
explain: 'Call back' means to phone again. 'Didn't' is the short form of 'did not'.
usage: Use it to share disappointment about no reply.
leelaQ: What do you do if no one replies to your message?
answer: I wait one day and then call them again.

en: I have learnt to ride a bicycle, and now I ride it daily.
tamil: நான் சைக்கிள் ஓட்ட கத்துக்கிட்டேன், இப்போ தினமும் ஓட்டுறேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a new skill.
explain: Present perfect shows a result that matters now. The result here is daily riding.
usage: Use it to talk proudly about a skill you picked up.
leelaQ: What new skill have you learnt recently?
answer: I have learnt to cook rice and sambar.

en: What did your mother say when she saw the marks?
tamil: மார்க்கை பார்த்ததும் உங்க அம்மா என்ன சொன்னாங்க?
context: Asking a friend about a school result story.
explain: 'When' joins two past events in a question.
usage: Use it to ask a friend about their family's reaction.
leelaQ: What did your parents say when you passed an exam?
answer: They were very happy and gave me sweets.

en: My father gave me a watch on my tenth birthday.
tamil: எனக்கு பத்தாவது பிறந்தநாளுக்கு அப்பா ஒரு கடிகாரம் கொடுத்தார்.
context: Sharing a memory about a gift.
explain: 'Gave' is the past of 'give'. 'On my tenth birthday' tells the exact time.
usage: Use it to tell a happy memory about your family.
leelaQ: What was the best gift you got as a child?
answer: I got a new cycle on my birthday.

en: Have you ever missed a flight?
tamil: நீங்க எப்பவாவது ஃபிளைட்டை மிஸ் பண்ணிருக்கீங்களா?
context: Chatting with a friend about travel problems.
explain: Use 'Have you ever' and the past participle 'missed' to ask about a life experience.
usage: Use it to start a talk about travel stories.
leelaQ: Have you ever missed a train or bus? What did you do?
answer: Yes, I missed a train and took the next one.

en: We waited in the queue for two hours, but the counter closed.
tamil: ரெண்டு மணி நேரம் வரிசையில நின்னோம், ஆனா கவுண்ட்டர் மூடிட்டாங்க.
context: Complaining to a friend about a bad experience.
explain: 'But' shows a bad surprise after a long effort.
usage: Use it to tell a frustrating experience at a bank or office.
leelaQ: What do you do when you wait too long in a queue?
answer: I read news on my phone and wait patiently.

en: Please don't stop, tell me the rest of the story.
tamil: நிறுத்தாதீங்க, மீதி கதையை சொல்லுங்க.
context: Encouraging a friend to continue.
explain: 'Don't stop' is a negative imperative. 'The rest' means the remaining part.
usage: Use it while a story is getting interesting.
leelaQ: Do you like listening to stories? Why?
answer: Yes, I like them because they are interesting.

en: The little boy hid behind the door and scared his sister.
tamil: அந்த சின்ன பையன் கதவுக்கு பின்னாடி ஒளிஞ்சுக்கிட்டு தன் தங்கச்சியை பயமுறுத்தினான்.
context: Telling a funny story about children.
explain: 'Hid' is the past of 'hide'. 'Scared' means made someone afraid.
usage: Use it to tell a funny family story about kids.
leelaQ: Did you play tricks on your brother or sister?
answer: Yes, I hid her slippers and she kept searching.

en: We didn't go out yesterday because of the heavy rain.
tamil: பெருமழை காரணமா நேத்து நாங்க வெளியே போகல.
context: Telling a friend why you stayed at home.
explain: 'Didn't go' is the negative past. Use 'because of' with a noun.
usage: Use it to explain why you cancelled a plan.
leelaQ: What do you do at home on a rainy day?
answer: I watch movies and drink hot tea.

en: It was raining heavily, so we stood under a tree for some time.
tamil: பலமா மழை பெய்துக்கிட்டு இருந்துச்சு, அதனால கொஞ்ச நேரம் மரத்துக்கு கீழ நின்னோம்.
context: Describing a rainy day to a friend.
explain: Past continuous (was raining) sets the background of a story.
usage: Use it to describe the weather at the time of an event.
leelaQ: What do you do when it suddenly rains outside?
answer: I stand in a shop and wait till it stops.

en: Did the train leave on time?
tamil: ரயில் சரியான நேரத்துக்கு கிளம்புச்சா?
context: Asking a family member who went to the station.
explain: 'On time' means at the right time. 'Leave' stays in base form after 'did'.
usage: Use it to ask about arrival or departure of any transport.
leelaQ: Does the bus in your area come on time?
answer: No, it is usually ten minutes late.

en: I got my first salary in 2019 and bought a gift for my mother.
tamil: நான் 2019ல முதல் சம்பளம் வாங்கி அம்மாவுக்கு ஒரு பரிசு வாங்கினேன்.
context: Talking about your first job.
explain: Use 'in' with a year. Two past actions are joined with 'and'.
usage: Use it to share a proud memory at work or with family.
leelaQ: What did you do with your first salary?
answer: I gave it to my parents and bought sweets.

en: Where were you born, and where did you grow up?
tamil: நீங்க எங்க பிறந்தீங்க, எங்க வளர்ந்தீங்க?
context: Getting to know a new colleague.
explain: 'Were you born' uses 'be' in the past. 'Did you grow up' uses 'did' plus a base verb.
usage: Use it politely to learn about someone's hometown.
leelaQ: Where were you born and where did you grow up?
answer: I was born in Trichy and grew up in Chennai.

en: She has changed her job twice since she moved to Bangalore.
tamil: அவ பெங்களூர் போனதுல இருந்து ரெண்டு தடவை வேலை மாத்தியிருக்கா.
context: Telling a friend about a relative's career.
explain: 'Since' plus a past event shows the starting point of the time period.
usage: Use it to give news about someone's life.
leelaQ: Has any of your friends moved to another city?
answer: Yes, my friend has moved to Hyderabad for work.

en: Can you share your trip photos with me?
tamil: உங்க டிரிப் போட்டோக்களை எனக்கு ஷேர் பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend after a group trip.
explain: 'Share with me' means send to me. 'Can you' is a casual request.
usage: Use it after a trip or a function to ask for pictures.
leelaQ: Do you take many photos on your trips?
answer: Yes, I take lots of photos of places and food.

en: The teacher scolded the whole class because somebody broke the window.
tamil: யாரோ ஜன்னலை உடைச்சதால டீச்சர் முழு கிளாஸையும் திட்டினாங்க.
context: Remembering a school incident.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason for something that happened.
usage: Use it to tell school stories to friends or children.
leelaQ: Do you remember any funny moment from school?
answer: Yes, our teacher fell asleep in the class once.

en: I have never been so embarrassed in my life.
tamil: என் வாழ்க்கையில இவ்ளோ அவமானப்பட்டதே இல்ல.
context: Telling a friend about a very awkward moment.
explain: 'Have never been' talks about the whole life up to now.
usage: Use it to describe a really awkward moment you went through.
leelaQ: Can you tell me about an embarrassing moment?
answer: I once called my teacher 'mom' in front of the class.

en: I woke up late, had a quick bath, and ran to the bus stop.
tamil: லேட்டா எந்திரிச்சேன், அவசரமா குளிச்சுட்டு பஸ் ஸ்டாப்புக்கு ஓடினேன்.
context: Describing a rushed morning.
explain: Several past actions in a row are separated with commas and 'and'.
usage: Use it to describe your morning to a friend or colleague.
leelaQ: How was your morning today?
answer: I woke up early, did yoga, and had breakfast.

en: What was the funniest thing that happened in your school?
tamil: உங்க ஸ்கூல்ல நடந்த காமெடியான விஷயம் என்ன?
context: Asking a friend for a funny story.
explain: 'The funniest thing that happened' uses the superlative and past tense together.
usage: Use it to start a fun chat with friends.
leelaQ: Can you share a funny incident from your school days?
answer: Our teacher once came to class with two different shoes.

en: My neighbour has helped us a lot since we moved here.
tamil: நாங்க இங்க வந்ததுல இருந்து எங்க பக்கத்து வீட்டுக்காரர் நிறைய உதவி பண்ணியிருக்கார்.
context: Thanking or praising a neighbour to others.
explain: Present perfect shows help that started in the past and still matters.
usage: Use it to speak kindly about someone who supported you.
leelaQ: Who has helped you the most in your life?
answer: My elder sister has helped me a lot in my studies.

en: And then what happened?
tamil: அப்புறம் என்ன ஆச்சு?
context: Encouraging a friend to continue a story.
explain: A short question that shows you are interested in the story.
usage: Use it while someone is telling you a story to keep them going.
leelaQ: When your friend tells a story, what do you ask?
answer: I ask, then what happened?

en: When the bell rang, all the children ran out of the class.
tamil: மணி அடிச்சதும் எல்லா குழந்தைகளும் கிளாஸை விட்டு ஓடினாங்க.
context: Describing a school scene.
explain: 'When' joins two events that happened one after another.
usage: Use it to describe a scene or event in a story.
leelaQ: What did you do when the school bell rang?
answer: I ran to the ground to play with my friends.
